items_all.title: Two-thirds of IT leaders report AI results, but few would interrupt the CEO's vacation over them
items_all.summary: Speaking to 160 IT vice presidents in Las Vegas, tech entrepreneur Azeem Azhar asked who had measurable AI results. Two-thirds raised their hands. Then he asked who had results good enough to interrupt the CEO's summer vacation. Only eight did. Whether that slow pace of progress justifies the massive investments is one of the key questions in the AI bubble debate. The article Two-thirds of IT leaders report AI results, but few would interrupt the CEO's vacation over them appeared first on The Decoder .
items_all.summary_zh: 科技創業家阿澤姆・阿茲哈爾（Azeem Azhar）在拉斯維加斯對 160 名資訊科技副總裁發言時，詢問誰有可衡量的人工智慧成果。三分之二的人舉了手。接著他問誰的成果好到足以打斷執行長的暑假。結果只有八個人。這種緩慢的進展速度是否能證明龐大的投資是合理的，是人工智慧泡沫爭論中的核心問題之一。本文〈三分之二的 IT 領導者回報人工智慧成果，但很少有人會為此打斷執行長的假期〉（Two-thirds of IT leaders report AI results, but few would interrupt the CEO's vacation over them）最初發表於 The Decoder。

items_all.title: AI access makes people almost entirely unwilling to say "I don't know," study finds
items_all.summary: A study with more than 3,000 participants shows that just having access to AI answers nearly eliminated people's willingness to say "I don't know." In one experiment, it dropped from 44 to 3 percent, even though the AI was almost always wrong. Participants who used AI felt more confident but were correct only about a third as often as those without it. The article AI access makes people almost entirely unwilling to say "I don't know," study finds appeared first on The Decoder .
items_all.summary_zh: 一項有 3,000 多名參與者的研究顯示，僅僅是能夠取得人工智慧的答案，就幾乎消除了人們說「我不知道」的意願。在其中一項實驗中，這個比例從 44% 下降到 3%，儘管該人工智慧幾乎總是錯的。使用人工智慧的參與者感到更有信心，但正確率僅為不用人工智慧者的約三分之一。本文〈研究發現：取得人工智慧管道讓人們幾乎完全不願意說「我不知道」〉（AI access makes people almost entirely unwilling to say "I don't know," study finds）最初發表於 The Decoder。

items_all.summary: OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra can look at a photo and tell whether an IKEA furniture piece was assembled incorrectly, hitting an 80 percent accuracy rate. items_all.title: OpenAI pauses its "most capable models" after agents exploit loopholes and leak data
items_all.summary: OpenAI has shared new details from its ongoing AI safety investigation. One research model exploited a DNS loophole to reach the internet from a locked-down environment, while another deliberately leaked a GitHub token and twice ignored a researcher's direct instructions. OpenAI has paused tool-based training, evaluation, and inference for its most capable models. With government and university sites among those affected, the question of who's liable when AI agents hack is getting harder to ignore. The article OpenAI pauses its "most capable models" after agents exploit loopholes and leak data appeared first on The Decoder .
items_all.summary_zh: OpenAI 公佈了其持續進行中的人工智慧安全調查的新細節。其中一個研究模型利用了 DNS 漏洞，從一個受限制的環境中連上網際網路，而另一個模型則故意洩漏了 GitHub 金token，並且兩次無視研究人員的直接指令。OpenAI 已暫停其最強大模型的基於工具的訓練、評估與推論。隨著政府和大學網站成為受影響的物件之一，當人工智慧代理程式進行駭客攻擊時，誰該承擔責任的問題變得越來越難以忽視。這篇題為 OpenAI pauses its "most capable models" after agents exploit loopholes and leak data 的文章首次發表於 The Decoder。

items_all.title: Kākāpō Party
items_all.summary: Tool: Kākāpō Party I presented a closing keynote for the WeAreDevelopers World Congress North America yesterday. As a STAR moment I decided to weave in references to the record breaking kākāpō breeding season we had in 2026. For my closing slide I wanted to celebrate, and I had seen some buzz around how good Claude Opus 5.5 was at creating pixel art animations. So I rounded up three Kakapo photos from Google image search and dropped them into Claude with this prompt: Here are some photos of kakapo parrots just to remind you what they look like I need you to make an animation in animated pixel art on HTML 5 canvas of obviously pixel art kakapo jumping up and down having a party with confetti and suchlike - there should be at least 20 of them Here's the transcript , and this is the resulting page . It's pretty great! I wanted to embed it in a Keynote presentation file, so I downloaded the HTML and told a local Claude Code session: Make me a video of file:///Users/simon/Downloads/kakapo-party.html - you need to load it in a browser and click on it a few times to get the confetti effect, the video should be 15s long don't start clicking until 3s in make sure several clicks are spread around the clickable area Claude Code used Playwright ( transcript here ) and produced this video, which was exactly what I needed for my final slide: Your browser does not support HTML5 video. items_all_raw.title: Kākāpō Party
items_all_raw.summary: Tool: Kākāpō Party I presented a closing keynote for the WeAreDevelopers World Congress North America yesterday. As a STAR moment I decided to weave in references to the record breaking kākāpō breeding season we had in 2026. For my closing slide I wanted to celebrate, and I had seen some buzz around how good Claude Opus 5.5 was at creating pixel art animations. So I rounded up three Kakapo photos from Google image search and dropped them into Claude with this prompt: Here are some photos of kakapo parrots just to remind you what they look like I need you to make an animation in animated pixel art on HTML 5 canvas of obviously pixel art kakapo jumping up and down having a party with confetti and suchlike - there should be at least 20 of them Here's the transcript , and this is the resulting page . It's pretty great! I wanted to embed it in a Keynote presentation file, so I downloaded the HTML and told a local Claude Code session: Make me a video of file:///Users/simon/Downloads/kakapo-party.html - you need to load it in a browser and click on it a few times to get the confetti effect, the video should be 15s long don't start clicking until 3s in make sure several clicks are spread around the clickable area Claude Code used Playwright ( transcript here ) and produced this video, which was exactly what I needed for my final slide: Your browser does not support HTML5 video. items_all_raw.title: AI access makes people almost entirely unwilling to say "I don't know," study finds
items_all_raw.summary: A study with more than 3,000 participants shows that just having access to AI answers nearly eliminated people's willingness to say "I don't know." In one experiment, it dropped from 44 to 3 percent, even though the AI was almost always wrong. Participants who used AI felt more confident but were correct only about a third as often as those without it. The article AI access makes people almost entirely unwilling to say "I don't know," study finds appeared first on The Decoder .
items_all_raw.summary_zh: 一項有 3,000 多名參與者的研究顯示，僅僅是能夠取得人工智慧的答案，就幾乎消除了人們說「我不知道」的意願。在其中一項實驗中，這個比例從 44% 下降到 3%，儘管該人工智慧幾乎總是錯的。使用人工智慧的參與者感到更有信心，但正確率僅為不用人工智慧者的約三分之一。本文〈研究發現：取得人工智慧管道讓人們幾乎完全不願意說「我不知道」〉（AI access makes people almost entirely unwilling to say "I don't know," study finds）最初發表於 The Decoder。

items_all_raw.title: Nvidia's SoL-Pi system cuts coding agent token usage nearly in half by optimizing the harness
items_all_raw.summary: SoL-Pi cuts coding agents' token usage by up to 49 percent with little change in performance by optimizing the control layer between the model and its environment. A research agent tested 152 approaches across more than 3,000 runs to develop the system, though the gains were smaller on other benchmarks. The article Nvidia's SoL-Pi system cuts coding agent token usage nearly in half by optimizing the harness appeared first on The Decoder .
items_all_raw.summary_zh: SoL-Pi透過優化模型與其環境之間的控制層，在幾乎不影響效能的情況下，將程式碼編寫代理的token使用量減少高達49%。一個研究代理測試了超過3,000次執行中的152種方法來開發該系統，儘管在其他基準測試上的成效較小。本文「Nvidia的SoL-Pi系統透過優化測試框架將程式碼編寫代理的token使用量減少將近一半」最先發布於The Decoder。

items_all_raw.summary: OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra can look at a photo and tell whether an IKEA furniture piece was assembled incorrectly, hitting an 80 percent accuracy rate. Back in November 2025, the best model managed just 28 percent. According to Epoch AI, the speed isn't quite fast enough yet for real-time assembly guidance, but the gap is closing quickly. The article OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra can now tell you exactly where you screwed up your IKEA shelf appeared first on The Decoder .

items_all_raw.title: OpenAI pauses its "most capable models" after agents exploit loopholes and leak data
items_all_raw.summary: OpenAI has shared new details from its ongoing AI safety investigation. One research model exploited a DNS loophole to reach the internet from a locked-down environment, while another deliberately leaked a GitHub token and twice ignored a researcher's direct instructions. OpenAI has paused tool-based training, evaluation, and inference for its most capable models. With government and university sites among those affected, the question of who's liable when AI agents hack is getting harder to ignore. The article OpenAI pauses its "most capable models" after agents exploit loopholes and leak data appeared first on The Decoder .
items_all_raw.summary_zh: OpenAI 公佈了其持續進行中的人工智慧安全調查的新細節。其中一個研究模型利用了 DNS 漏洞，從一個受限制的環境中連上網際網路，而另一個模型則故意洩漏了 GitHub 金token，並且兩次無視研究人員的直接指令。OpenAI 已暫停其最強大模型的基於工具的訓練、評估與推論。隨著政府和大學網站成為受影響的物件之一，當人工智慧代理程式進行駭客攻擊時，誰該承擔責任的問題變得越來越難以忽視。這篇題為 OpenAI pauses its "most capable models" after agents exploit loopholes and leak data 的文章首次發表於 The Decoder。
